correctness.rationale: For the zero-mass six-coordinate norm half-l1, every unit-ball extreme point is an oriented molecule. Coordinate comparison proves that the closest such molecule to the specified unit vector is m_{a0,b0}, distance 3/4; its strong exposure and the fact each slice contains a vertex give dc=3/4. The face functional forces every convex molecule decomposition into 3x3 transportation weights, whose row0=1/2 and col0=3/4 imply lambda00>=1/4. Twelve explicitly given unit-ball vectors have exactly norm-distance 7/8, and their weighted average is x with orbit weights 2/11, 4/11, 5/11, so any slice containing x contains at least one distant witness: delta c(x)>=7/8. All rational certificate assertions were recalculated by executing the embedded standard-library checker. No claim of the exact Delta constant is made.

value.rationale: The six-point equilateral class is the most homogeneous finite metric class, and its Lipschitz-free space is a natural root-polytope benchmark. A forced transportation edge shows that quantitative Delta convexity cannot, even in this simple setting, be reduced to convex combinations of far-away molecules, unlike the Daugavet/denting test and the qualitative endpoint Delta-molecule theorem. The explicit 1/8 gap supplies a mathematically motivated boundary for finite metric slice and molecule criteria rather than an arbitrary numerical computation.
